title: Five things that moved private markets.
intro: Five source-backed developments from the most recently completed week, with the valuation context that matters for private-market investors.

items.text: Bloomberg reported that OpenAI was weighing a new financing that could value it above $1.2 trillion, a discussion rather than a completed round. The importance is the scale of capital now being contemplated for frontier AI: private financing and secondary pricing are doing work once reserved for public markets.

Anthropic’s latest disclosed financing remains its $65 billion Series H at a $965 billion post-money valuation, which the company said followed a $47 billion revenue run rate. Alongside OpenAI’s reported financing talks, it makes clear that the frontier-model market is being priced as strategic infrastructure, not ordinary software.

Crusoe announced a $3.9 billion Series F at a $30.9 billion valuation, with the capital earmarked for large data-center projects and modular AI factories. The round is a concrete signal that power, land, and deployment capacity are becoming investable bottlenecks in the AI stack.

Profound raised a $180 million Series D at a $1.8 billion valuation for software that helps brands measure and improve their presence in AI-generated answers. It is an early but meaningful bet on the commercial layer around AI search, where budgets may shift before the underlying model market stabilizes.

May Mobility agreed to merge with a SPAC in a transaction that the company said values it at $1.4 billion and could provide more than $300 million of gross proceeds. The deal offers a useful read-through on whether public investors will fund an asset-light, partnership-led robotaxi strategy rather than only the largest autonomy platforms.
